inputs.text: On 25 March 2026, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement in Paris to design the Dominican Republic’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Luis Abinader present. That may sound impressive, but a foreign seal of approval is no substitute for honest officials and sound institutions. The strategy must serve the Dominican people, protect the rule of law, and hold public servants accountable—without letting international bureaucrats turn “integrity” into a cover for political interference or weakened national authority. The measure of success is whether it restores trust through fair, effective institutions at home.
